name: P21

lead: P21 is a small peptide derived from CNTF, a neurotrophic protein. It is discussed as a nootropic aimed at memory and focus.
Animal studies reported increased neurogenesis and better memory in aged and Alzheimer-model mice. People in nootropic communities use it for cognition and long-term brain support.

paras: The compound is described in the research literature as a neurogenic and neurotrophic peptide that raises BDNF-related signaling and supports synapses and new neurons in the dentate gyrus.
No approved human use exists, and published work is in animals and cells. It is a research compound, and gray-market products are not regulated as medicines.

chain: Studied for neurogenesis and BDNF signalling in mice
Used by enthusiasts for focus and cognition
angle.text: Users take P21 as a nootropic peptide aimed at memory and focus, which supports study, work and training. Its link to appearance runs through that general performance and well-being theme rather than through any direct effect on the body.

lead: P21 (also written P021) is a short synthetic peptide designed from a region of ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF), a protein that supports nerve cells. In peptide and nootropic circles it is discussed as a cognitive-support compound, with interest in memory, focus and long-term brain health. People attach it to appearance goals only indirectly, through the idea that sharper focus and brain health support study, work and training routines.[1][2]

Published work comes from laboratory and animal research, much of it from the group of Khalid Iqbal and colleagues. In 3xTg Alzheimer-model mice, P021 given from the prenatal or early postnatal period prevented cognitive impairment, raised the signalling molecules pCREB and BDNF, and in one study reduced tau hyperphosphorylation and amyloid plaque load by 22 months.[2] A 2016 review described P021 as a small-molecule neurotrophic mimetic that boosts neurogenesis and BDNF in preclinical work, and a 2022 review set out the case for it as an Alzheimer's candidate.[2]

Not every result has been positive. A 2024 study in a CDKL5 deficiency disorder model found that P021 corrected proliferation, survival and maturation deficits in cultured cells, but chronic treatment in mice did not raise BDNF or repair neuroanatomical defects, and behavioural benefit was limited.[2] No human trials were found. The name is easily confused with p21 (CDKN1A), an unrelated cell-cycle protein that dominates search results.[3]
infobox: Mice (Alzheimer, aging, Down syndrome, CDKL5 models)[2]

paras: P021 is described in the literature as a neurotrophic small-molecule peptide mimetic, built from the active region of CNTF so that it can act on nerve cells without the drawbacks of the whole protein.[2] In the animal studies it was typically given in the diet or by injection to mice rather than used as a purified drug product.

Preclinical findings summarised by the research groups include: prevention of dendritic and synaptic deficits and cognitive impairment, reduced cognitive ageing, rescue of memory deficits in Alzheimer and Down syndrome mouse models, and effects on neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus.[2] A 2020 study in Alzheimer's Research and Therapy reported that prenatal-to-early-postnatal treatment rescued cognition at 4 months and lowered tau hyperphosphorylation and amyloid load later in life in 3xTg-AD mice, and a 2021 study in the Journal of Alzheimer's Disease reported similar behavioural and synaptic benefits from dietary treatment from birth.[2] A 2026 study used diffusion MRI to look at brain microstructure after early P021 treatment in the same mouse model.[2]
The CDKL5 study of 2024 reported a more limited outcome in mice, as described above.[2]

P021 is not an approved medicine, and published safety data come from cells and animals. Products sold online as research peptides are not regulated as drugs, and their content has not been independently characterised in the sources consulted.
The p21 protein (CDKN1A, WAF1/CIP1) is a cell-cycle inhibitor involved in cancer biology and DNA repair; it is a separate topic, and many search results about 'p21 peptides' concern it.[3]
No studies found in humans. Animal and cell research is described above.[2]
